questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly uses inversion to emphasize the adverbial phrase.

A. Only after the rain stopped did the children go out to play.
B. Only after the rain stopped do the children go out to play.
C. Only after the rain stopped were the children going out to play.
D. Only after the rain stopped had the children gone out to play.
options: Only after the rain stopped did the children go out to play.
Only after the rain stopped do the children go out to play.
Only after the rain stopped were the children going out to play.
Only after the rain stopped had the children gone out to play.
questions.answer: Only after the rain stopped did the children go out to play.

questions.question:
Which of the following sentences correctly employs a cleft sentence to highlight the specific detail?

A. It was John who broke the window yesterday.
B. John broke the window yesterday, but it was not.
C. That John broke the window yesterday is clear.
D. Yesterday, the window was broken by John.
options: It was John who broke the window yesterday.
John broke the window yesterday, but it was not.
That John broke the window yesterday is clear.
Yesterday, the window was broken by John.
questions.answer: It was John who broke the window yesterday.

questions.question:
Select the correct form of the conditional sentence that expresses a hypothetical situation in the past with a likely outcome.

A. If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
B. If I had studied harder, I would pass the exam.
C. If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
D. If I had studied harder, I will have passed the exam.
options: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I had studied harder, I would pass the exam.
If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I had studied harder, I will have passed the exam.
questions.answer: If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a formal recommendation?

A. I suggest that the committee members attend the meeting.
B. I suggest that the committee members attend the meeting.
C. I suggest that the committee members attending the meeting.
D. I suggest that the committee members should attend the meeting.
options: I suggest that the committee members attend the meeting.
I suggest that the committee members attend the meeting.
I suggest that the committee members attending the meeting.
I suggest that the committee members should attend the meeting.
questions.answer: I suggest that the committee members attend the meeting.

questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly demonstrates ellipsis, omitting the understood words.

A. She likes coffee, and so does he.
B. She likes coffee, and he does too.
C. She likes coffee, and he also does.
D. She likes coffee, and he likes it too.
options: She likes coffee, and so does he.
She likes coffee, and he does too.
She likes coffee, and he also does.
She likes coffee, and he likes it too.
questions.answer: She likes coffee, and so does he.
